笛子屬氣鳴橫吹樂器，吹氣切過吹孔邊棱後，部分氣流進入管內，使空氣柱依管腔直徑與長: The dizi is a transverse aerophone: the breath cuts across the edge of the blowhole, part of the airstream goes into the tube, and the air column resonates according to the diameter and length of the bore to give the pitch. The key to its timbre is the membrane hole between the blowhole and the fingerholes: with the dizi membrane pasted on, the resonance is brighter and louder and gains overtones, giving a nasal, buzzing quality. Its range is about two and a quarter octaves. Beside the xindi, which has no membrane hole, and the xiao or koudi, the dizi sounds sharper and brighter because of its membrane; the bangdi and qudi, of different bore and length, give a high strident tone and a rounder one respectively.
笛子常見於中國民間音樂、戲曲與民族樂團，也用於交響樂團和現代音樂。北方梆笛多伴奏: The dizi is common in Chinese folk music, opera and the Chinese orchestra, and is also used in symphony orchestras and modern music. The northern bangdi mostly accompanies bangzi opera and appears in local music such as errentai; the southern qudi often leads kunqu and Jiangnan sizhu. The xindi takes a mediating part in the modern Chinese orchestra. For listening, one can choose Tan Dun's 《竹跡》 (“Bamboo Traces”), Yang Qing's 《醉笛》 (“Drunken Flute”), Mo Fan's 《綠洲》 (“Oasis”), Li Bochan's 《熱情與冷漠的邂逅》 and 《竹石》 (“Bamboo and Stone”), and Liu Sen's arrangements for dizi of 《霍拉舞曲》 (the “Hora”), Rimsky-Korsakov's 《野蜂飛舞》 (“Flight of the Bumblebee”) and the 《單簧管波爾卡》 (“Clarinet Polka”).
笛子是中國傳統吹管樂器，以竹子製成，音色清脆明亮。: The dizi is a traditional Chinese wind instrument, made of bamboo, with a bright, clear timbre.
笛子琴身多以竹製成，主要用苦竹與紫竹，近來亦見湘妃竹；北方常見紫竹或紫色竹，蘇州: The body of the dizi is mostly bamboo, mainly ku bamboo and purple bamboo, with mottled bamboo also seen lately; in the north purple or purplish bamboo is common, around Suzhou and Hangzhou white bamboo is mostly used, and in the south, around Chaozhou, a fine, light, pale bamboo. There are also instruments of other woods or of stone; jade dizi are mostly for collectors or for those who care about appearance, but they do not resonate as well as bamboo. It does not sound with a reed but with the airstream cutting the edge of the blowhole and the air column in the tube resonating; the membrane hole takes a dizi membrane, which can be bamboo membrane, gut membrane or reed membrane, nowadays mostly reed. In modern times, to adjust the pitch, brass joints have been used to join two sections of bamboo. The making involves lacquering and binding with thread, though the source does not state the materials of the lacquer and the thread.
笛子（Dizi）是中國橫吹氣鳴樂器，Hornbostel–Sachs 編號 42: The dizi is a Chinese transverse aerophone, Hornbostel–Sachs 421.121.12. The body is mostly bamboo, with a blowhole, fingerholes and a membrane hole; the membrane hole takes a dizi membrane, and when it is played the airstream cuts the edge of the blowhole and the air column in the tube resonates. It is widely used in Chinese folk music, opera and the modern Chinese orchestra; the northern bangdi is common in bangzi opera and errentai, and the southern qudi in kunqu and Jiangnan sizhu.
考古資料顯示，中國簡單橫吹笛已有九千餘年，賈湖遺址出土公元前七千至五千年骨笛，具: Archaeological evidence shows that simple transverse flutes have existed in China for more than nine thousand years; bone flutes dated 7000 to 5000 BC from the Jiahu site have five to eight holes and can play about an octave. The dizi in its present form begins around the fifth century BC, and bamboo flutes are known from the second century BC. The dizi originally had no membrane; the membrane may have come about because covering a spare hole made the timbre brighter, and reed membrane later came into general use. The fingerholes were at first evenly spaced and were moved to adjust the semitones; in the 1920s Zheng Jinwen added brass joints for fine tuning, and in the middle of the twentieth century the holes were moved again to suit equal temperament. In the 1930s the eleven-hole xindi appeared. The Tang dynasty shakuhachi later passed to Japan, and in modern times the dizi has entered the Chinese orchestra and the solo repertoire.
